lines.japanese: 「ね、ちょっと…」
lines.english: “Hey, look…”
“Hm? What is it?”

lines.japanese:
「ほら、向こう。大学の正門とこ。
ウチの制服着てる…」
lines.english: “Over there, by the university’s main gate. That girl in our uniform…”

lines.japanese:
「あの人…？
確か三年の…ああ！」
lines.english: “Her…? Isn’t she that senior… Oh!”

lines.japanese:
「だよね？　やっぱりあの人だよね？
よかった、見間違いじゃなかったんだ」
lines.english: “Right? It is her, isn’t it? Good—I thought I might be seeing things.”

lines.japanese: 「相手がウチの大学の人って噂、本当だったんだ…」
lines.english: “So the rumor about her dating someone from our university was true…”

lines.japanese:
「いや本当助かった！
語学系はなかなかノート揃わなくてさぁ」
lines.english:
“Seriously, you saved my ass!
It’s hard to get a full set of notes for language classes.”

lines.japanese: 「…いい加減、他学部にまで借りに来るのはやめろ」
lines.english: “…Stop coming all the way to other departments to borrow them.”

lines.japanese:
昨夜、日付の変わり目くらいにかかってきた電話は、
『春希、明日フランス語のノート持ってきてくんね？』
という、非常にフレンドリーなものだった。
lines.english: The call had come around midnight last night, with a remarkably casual: “Haruki, bring me your French notes tomorrow, would you?”

lines.japanese:
「お前が勝手に転部するから悪いんだろ。
おかげで俺の成績にどれほどの悪影響が出たか、
真面目に考えたことあるのか？」
lines.english: “It’s your fault for switching departments without consulting me. Have you ever seriously considered how much damage that’s done to my grades?”

lines.japanese:
「…まずは試験を自分の実力で受けることを
真面目に考えろ」
lines.english: “…First, seriously consider taking your exams on your own merits.”

lines.japanese:
…着信を見ずに通話ボタンを押してしまった俺は、
数秒間凍りついてしまったけれど、それはまた別の話。
lines.english: I’d answered without looking at the caller ID and spent several seconds frozen, but that was another story.

lines.japanese:
「さて、と…
今日これからどうする？」
lines.english: “Well, then… What are you doing after this?”

lines.japanese: 「帰ってすぐに勉強に決まってるだろ」
lines.english: “Going straight home to study, obviously.”

lines.japanese:
「…なんという模範的で面白くない回答。
相変わらず大学生らしくないな」
lines.english: “…What an exemplary, utterly boring answer. You still haven’t learned how to be a college student.”

lines.japanese:
「…つい今しがたまで
随分と無駄な時間を浪費させてもらったからな」
lines.english: “…You’ve already made me waste a staggering amount of perfectly useless time.”

lines.japanese:
試験が終わった後向かったコピー機前の大行列は、
そこに並ぶデメリットしかない俺を大いに嘆かせた。
lines.english: The enormous line at the copier after the exam made me bitterly regret being there, since I had absolutely nothing to gain by waiting in it.

lines.japanese:
「…無駄な時間なら浪費してもいいじゃん？
何言ってんのお前」
lines.english: “…If the time was useless, what’s wrong with wasting it? What are you complaining about?”

lines.japanese:
「ああっ！？
お前、修飾関係をわざとミスリードすんのやめろ！
俺が紛らわしい言い方したみたいじゃないか！」
lines.english: “What the hell? Stop deliberately parsing it the wrong way! Now you make it sound like I was the one who phrased it badly!”

lines.japanese:
「いや実際紛らわしかったんだって。
…礼と詫びの意味で晩飯おごろうと思ってたんだけどな」
lines.english: “You did phrase it ambiguously. I was going to buy you dinner as thanks—and an apology.”

lines.japanese:
「じゃあ『貴重な時間を浪費』に言い直す。
…飯は試験終わってからに取っとくわ」
lines.english: “Fine, I amend that to ‘wasting valuable time.’ Dinner can wait until exams are over.”

lines.japanese:
「土日空いてんだから今日くらいいいだろ。
軽く飲まね？」
lines.english: “You’ve got the whole weekend free. You can spare tonight. Come have a couple drinks.”

lines.japanese:
「俺はどっちかって言うと来週からが本命なんだよ。
まだ９科目残ってるし。月曜なんか３科目だぞ」
lines.english: “Next week is the real battle for me. I still have nine exams left—three on Monday alone.”

lines.japanese:
「…お前、もうとっくに卒業できる単位数揃えてるだろ。
後は趣味の世界だよな、それ」
lines.english: “…You’ve had enough credits to graduate for ages. At this point, you’re doing it for fun.”

lines.japanese:
「何とでも言え。
とにかく今から月曜の朝までずっと勉強。
でなけりゃ各方面に申し訳が立たん」
lines.english: “Say what you like. I’m studying from now until Monday morning. Otherwise I couldn’t face all the people counting on me.”

lines.japanese:
…特に、今週末バイトに来ないと知って、
思いっきり声のトーンを落とした後、
慌てて必死に明るく振舞った彼女とかに…
lines.english: …Especially the girl whose voice had plummeted when she learned I wouldn’t be working this weekend, before she hurriedly forced herself to sound cheerful again…

lines.japanese:
…そうだ。
週末、グッディーズで勉強しようか。
帰り道だけ、ほんの少し足を伸ばして電車を使おうか。
lines.english: Actually… maybe I could study at Goodies this weekend. It would only mean going a little out of my way and taking the train home.

lines.japanese:
そしたら彼女は
『店内は勉強する場所じゃありません』
なんて、嬉しそうに説教してくれるだろうか…
lines.english: Would she beam at me while scolding, “This restaurant is not a study hall”?

lines.japanese:
「あと一週間かぁ…
早く終わんねぇかなぁ」
lines.english: “One more week… God, I wish it would hurry up and end.”

lines.japanese: 「…そうだな」
lines.english: “…Yeah.”

lines.japanese:
そういえば昨夜は、本来電話が掛かってくるべき時間に
俺が話し中だったせいか、結局、着信画面に
『杉浦小春』という文字列が表示されることはなかった。
lines.english: Come to think of it, I’d been on the phone at the time she normally called last night, and the name “Koharu Sugiura” had never appeared on my screen.

lines.japanese:
待つのに疲れて寝てしまったのか、
毎晩電話するのに飽きてしまったのか…
lines.english: Maybe she’d grown tired of waiting and gone to sleep. Maybe she’d grown tired of calling me every night…

lines.japanese:
それとも、俺の声を聞かなくても済むくらい、
学校で楽しいことでもあったのか…
lines.english: Or maybe something good had happened at school—something good enough that she hadn’t needed to hear my voice…

lines.japanese:
まぁ、どれでもいいか。
その逆でさえなければ、なんでも…
lines.english: Any of those would be fine. Anything, as long as the truth wasn’t the opposite…

lines.japanese:
「そいやさ、お前…
来週の雪菜ちゃんとこのパーティは行くのか？」
lines.english: “Oh, right. Are you going to that party at Setsuna’s next week?”

lines.japanese: 「…お前んとこにも誘い来たのか？」
lines.english: “…She invited you too?”

lines.japanese: 「二人っきりが良かったか？」
lines.english: “Were you hoping to have her all to yourself?”

lines.japanese:
「何言ってんだ…
もともと家族が一緒だろ」
lines.english: “What are you talking about? Her family was always going to be there.”

lines.japanese:
「『お嬢さんを俺にください』を
やるつもりだったのかなって」
lines.english: “I thought maybe you were planning to do the whole ‘Sir, may I have your daughter’s hand?’ routine.”

lines.japanese: 「馬鹿なこと………言うな」
lines.english: “Don’t……… say something so stupid.”

lines.japanese:
ついさっきまで思い浮かべていたことと、
武也との会話の内容があまりに噛み合わず、
少しだけ頭がふらついた。
lines.english: What I’d been thinking about until a moment ago had so little to do with this conversation that my head swam.

lines.japanese:
「俺と依緒もお邪魔させてもらうことになってる。
何しろ雪菜ちゃんの手料理だぜ？
…主賓がケーキ焼く誕生パーティってのもなんだけど」
lines.english: “Io and I are going too. I mean, we get Setsuna’s home cooking. Though it’s a little weird making the birthday girl bake her own cake.”

lines.japanese: 「そ…っか」
lines.english: “Oh… I see.”

lines.japanese:
「来るよな？　春希。
断る理由ないだろ？
何しろ、これで本当にただのホームパーティだ」
lines.english: “You’re coming, right, Haruki? There’s no reason not to. With all of us there, it really is just a regular house party.”
“Takeya…?”

lines.japanese:
それは、誰が考えたのかわからないけれど、
…多分、雪菜じゃないことだけはわかるけれど。
lines.english: I didn’t know who had arranged that—though I was fairly sure it hadn’t been Setsuna.

lines.japanese:
俺がすごく乗りやすく、
そして、とても断りにくいイベントになっていた。
lines.english:
The party had been arranged so that it was easy for me
to say yes—and terribly hard to say no.

lines.japanese:
「旅行の相談とかもしたいしな。
お前、予定がないとすぐバイト入れちまうから」
lines.english: “We want to talk about the trip, too. Leave you with an empty day and you’ll fill it with work before anyone can stop you.”

lines.japanese:
「楽しみだな、春休み。
四年になったら遊ぶ暇なんかないだろうし、
今のうちに遊び溜めしとこうぜ？」
lines.english: “Spring break’s going to be great. Once we’re seniors, we won’t have time to screw around, so let’s get our fill now.”

lines.japanese: 「春休み…か」
lines.english: “Spring break…”

lines.japanese:
試験が終わったら。
三年生が終わったら。
lines.english: When exams were over. When our junior year was over.

lines.japanese: 冬が、終わったら…
lines.english: When winter was over…

lines.japanese:
俺は、どこに行き、
誰に気持ちを伝えるんだろう。
lines.english: Where would I go, and whom would I tell how I felt?

lines.japanese:
…誰を傷つけて、
何を壊してしまうんだろう。
lines.english: Whom would I hurt, and what would I destroy?
“What…?”

lines.japanese: 「武也？」
lines.english: “Takeya?”

lines.japanese:
俺が、しばらく下を向いて考え事にふけっていたら、
いつの間にか武也を追い抜いてしまっていた。
lines.english: I’d been walking with my head down, lost in thought, and passed Takeya without realizing it.

lines.japanese:
というか、武也が突然立ち止まり、
呆然と正門の方向を見て固まっていたという方が…
lines.english: Or rather, Takeya had stopped without warning and stood frozen, staring blankly toward the main gate.

lines.japanese:
「なんだよ武也？
一体どうし…」
lines.english: “What’s wrong, Takeya? What are you—”

lines.japanese:
武也の視線を追った瞬間…
俺も同じ表情を作ってしまっていた。
lines.english: The instant I followed his gaze, my face went as blank as his.

lines.japanese:
それだけじゃない。
その視線の先にいた人物も…
lines.english: And we weren’t the only ones. The person at the other end of that stare…

lines.japanese:
こちらを呆然と見つめ、
その後、急に落ち着きをなくしたように周囲を見回し、
そして、泣きそうな顔を作る。
lines.english: She stared back at us, stunned. Then, as if panic had suddenly seized her, she looked frantically around before her face crumpled on the verge of tears.

lines.japanese:
遠くからでもわかる、焦燥、悲壮、戸惑い。
そしてその表情が、俺の顔にも移っていくのがわかる。
lines.english: Even at that distance, I could see her desperation, her anguish, her confusion—and feel each of them spreading across my own face.

lines.japanese: どうして、ここに…
lines.english: Why was she here…?

lines.japanese: 「こは…」
lines.english: “Koha—”

lines.japanese:
「よ～小春ちゃんじゃん！
え～なになに？　俺に会いに来てくれたわけ～？」
lines.english: “Well, if it isn’t Koharu! What’s this? Did you come all this way to see me?”

lines.japanese:
先に発見した分、
武也の切り替えの方が一瞬だけ早かった。
lines.english: Because he had spotted her first, Takeya recovered a split second before I did.

lines.japanese:
それは、良かったのか悪かったのか、
結果的に俺の致命的なミスを覆い隠してくれてもくれた。
lines.english: For better or worse, that split second also concealed the disastrous mistake I had nearly made.

lines.japanese:
「こ～んなとこで寒かったでしょ。
なに、電話くれればすぐ迎えに行ったのに～」
lines.english: “You must’ve been freezing out here. Why didn’t you call? I’d have come straight down to get you.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、あ、あの…っ」

本当だよ。
電話くれれば、すぐに…
lines.english: He was right. If she’d called, I could have come straight down…

lines.japanese:
こんな目立つところで武也に見とがめられるより、
よっぽど上手い方法なんかいくらでも考えついたのに。
lines.english: I could have thought of any number of better ways to handle this than letting Takeya catch her waiting in the most conspicuous place imaginable.

lines.japanese:
「でもここで会うの久しぶりだよね～。
最初ほら、すっごい勢いでこっち睨んでてさぁ」
lines.english: “It’s been ages since we ran into you here. Remember the first time? You were glaring daggers at us.”

lines.japanese: 「ち、違うんです。その…違うんですよ！」
lines.english: “N-no, that’s not—I mean, you’ve got it wrong!”

lines.japanese:
武也の言葉に必死に応えながら、
目が必死に俺に訴えてる。
lines.english: She answered Takeya desperately, but her eyes were pleading just as desperately with me.

lines.japanese:
内容は、多分口で言ってるのと同じ。
『違うんです』
『こんなつもりじゃ、なかったんです』
lines.english:
Her eyes were probably saying the same thing as her mouth:
“This isn’t what it looks like.”
“I never meant for this to happen.”

lines.japanese:
ただ、口に出しているものとは、
その言葉の持つ意味が全然違うだけ…
lines.english: The words simply meant something entirely different when her eyes said them to me.

lines.japanese: 「俺らに用事じゃなかったの？」
lines.english: “So you weren’t here for us?”

lines.japanese:
「だから、用なんて何もないんです。
ただその、気がついたらこんなところに…」
lines.english: “I keep telling you, I wasn’t here for anything. I just… found myself here before I knew it.”

lines.japanese:
武也がいつの間にか選択肢に俺を取り込み、
どれだけ上手く誘導しても、
今の小春は、何も読むことができない。
lines.english: Takeya had quietly folded me into that “us,” but however deftly he tried to lead her, Koharu was in no state to catch a hint.

lines.japanese: 「誰か別の人でも待ってる？」
lines.english: “Are you waiting for somebody else?”

lines.japanese: 「…ないです。ごめんなさい」
lines.english: “…No one. I’m sorry.”

lines.japanese:
「いや、謝ることないけどさ。
むしろ俺たちとしては偶然でも嬉しいなって」
lines.english: “Nothing to apologize for. We’re glad we happened to find you.”

lines.japanese:
自分がしてしまった行動に、
何より一番、自分自身がついていけてない…
lines.english: More than anyone, Koharu herself seemed unable to process what she’d done…

lines.japanese: そんな感じだった。
lines.english: That was how it looked.

lines.japanese:
「そうだ、用がないんなら小春ちゃんも一緒に来ない？
俺たち、今から晩ご飯食べに行くとこだったんだ。
試験が折り返し地点に来た打ち上げも兼ねて」
lines.english: “Hey, if you’ve got nothing else going on, why not join us? We were about to get dinner. Call it a little celebration for reaching the halfway point of exams.”

lines.japanese:
「…いえ、いいです。ごめんなさい。
本当に、何の用もなかったんですから」
lines.english: “…No, thank you. I’m sorry. I truly didn’t come here for any reason.”

lines.japanese:
『そんな約束もしてないし、
折り返し地点に来たくらいで浮かれる訳にもいかないの』
lines.english: “We never made plans like that, and getting halfway through exams is no excuse to celebrate.”

lines.japanese:
…なんて、いつもなら、
説教臭い態度で突っ込みを入れなくちゃならないのに。
lines.english: Normally she would have cut in with some preachy retort like that.

lines.japanese:
「用事ないんならいいじゃん。
男二人だけが嫌なら依緒も呼ぶからさ？」
lines.english: “If you’ve got nothing else to do, come on. If you don’t want to be alone with two men, I’ll call Io.”

lines.japanese: 『だから俺はそんな約束…』
lines.english: ‘But I never agreed to any—’

lines.japanese: 「いえ………帰ります」
lines.english: “No……… I’m going home.”

lines.japanese:
「…そう？
残念だなぁ、せっかく明日休みだから、
ゆっくり遊べるのに」
lines.english: “…You are? That’s a shame. Tomorrow’s our day off—we could’ve taken our time.”

lines.japanese:
「先輩たち、試験期間中じゃないですか。
ゆっくり遊んでたら、駄目じゃないですか…」
lines.english: “You’re in the middle of exams. You can’t afford to be out having fun…”

lines.japanese:
「…痛いとこ突かないでよ。
さっき春希に同じこと言われたばかりだ」
lines.english: “…Right where it hurts. Haruki was telling me the same thing five minutes ago.”

lines.japanese:
「そうですよ。
暇なんか、ないんですよ………」
lines.english: “Exactly. You don’t have time to spare………”

lines.japanese: そして小春は俯き、言葉を失っていく。
lines.english: Koharu lowered her head, and the words left her.

lines.japanese:
まるで、自分の口から出た言葉に、
酷く傷ついたみたいに…
lines.english: As though the words from her own mouth had wounded her terribly…

lines.japanese:
「さよなら。
お疲れさまでした」
lines.english: “Goodbye. And good luck with your exams.”

lines.japanese:
「そう？　またね。
試験終わったらお店の方行くから」
lines.english: “All right. See you around. I’ll stop by the restaurant when exams are over.”

lines.japanese:
「お待ちしてます。
それじゃ…」
lines.english: “We’ll be looking forward to it. Well, then…”

lines.japanese:
「あ！
ごめん、すっかり忘れてた！」
lines.english: “Wait! I’m sorry—I completely forgot!”
“What…?”

lines.japanese: 「春希？」
lines.english: “Haruki?”

lines.japanese:
駄目だ、これは…
辻褄を、合わせないと。
lines.english:
This wouldn’t do…
I had to make the pieces fit.

lines.japanese:
「悪い！　完全に俺のチョンボ。
彼女、本当は俺と待ち合わせだったんだ」
lines.english: “Sorry! This is completely my fault. She was actually waiting for me.”
“Haruki…?”

lines.japanese:
小春の態度とか、今ここにいる事実とか、
そして、今の彼女の感情への対応とか。
lines.english: Koharu’s behavior. Her presence here. And what to do about everything she was feeling now.

lines.japanese:
「ち、違います！
わたし、先輩を待ってなんか…っ！」
lines.english: “Th-that’s not true! I wasn’t waiting for you!”

lines.japanese: 「…小春ちゃん？」
lines.english: “…Koharu?”

lines.japanese:
「確かに大遅刻した俺が悪いんだけど、
そうやっていつまでもむくれないでくれ…」
lines.english: “I know it’s my fault for being horribly late, but don’t keep sulking forever…”
“Wh-what are you…?”

lines.japanese:
…午前中の試験でオーバーヒートしたはずの俺の頭が、
一瞬で冷たさを取り戻していく。
lines.english: …My brain, supposedly overheated by the morning’s exams, went cold in an instant.

lines.japanese:
「先週のバイトの時約束したんだよ…
ウチのキャンパスを案内するって」
lines.english: “We arranged it at work last week. I promised to show her around campus.”

lines.japanese:
今の事態を受け、自分の中で優先度を並べ直し、
一番最適な『シナリオ』を組み上げていく。
lines.english:
I reordered my priorities in an instant
and began assembling the best possible “scenario.”

lines.japanese:
「先月、孝宏君を案内したことを話してたら、
自分も見てみたいって、そういう流れになってさ…」
lines.english: “I mentioned showing Takahiro around last month, and she said she’d like to see the place too. One thing led to another…”

lines.japanese: 小春がここで待っていたのは俺。
lines.english: Koharu had been waiting here for me.

lines.japanese:
けれどそれは、
単にバイト先の先輩と進学先の先輩が
同一人物だったからに過ぎない。
lines.english: But only because her more experienced coworker happened to be an upperclassman at the university she planned to attend.

lines.japanese: ついでに『クラスメートの姉の彼氏』も…
lines.english: And, incidentally, “her classmate’s older sister’s boyfriend,” too…

lines.japanese:
そして俺たちは、
『金曜日の放課後に正門前』という約束を交わし、
いつも通り、何事もなくバイト先で別れた。
lines.english: We’d agreed to meet “outside the main gate after school on Friday,” then parted at work as usual, with nothing untoward between us.

lines.japanese: そして今日、金曜日…
lines.english: And today was Friday.

lines.japanese:
約束通り、時間通りにやってきた小春。
後輩との約束“程度”のことなんかすっかり忘れ、
武也と構内をうろついていた俺。
lines.english: Koharu had arrived exactly when and where we’d agreed. I had completely forgotten something as trivial as a promise to a younger coworker and had been wandering around campus with Takeya.

lines.japanese:
当然、携帯番号なんか交換していないから、
連絡を取ることもできなかった。
lines.english: Naturally, we hadn’t exchanged phone numbers, so she’d had no way to reach me.

lines.japanese:
そして一時間以上も待たされた挙げ句、
その当の約束の相手が、
慌てもせずにいけしゃあしゃあと歩いてきたから…
lines.english: Then, after leaving her to wait for over an hour, the very person who had stood her up came strolling along without a care in the world.

lines.japanese:
小春はすっかりブチ切れて、
俺との約束なんかなかったみたいに振舞っていた。
lines.english: Koharu had understandably lost her temper and was pretending there had never been any promise between us.

lines.japanese:
「いや、本当にごめん！
この通り！」
lines.english: “I really am sorry! Look—I’m begging you!”

lines.japanese:
「少し遅くなったけど、
今からでも案内させてくれないかな？
…晩飯おごるから。学食だけど」
lines.english: “It’s late, but will you let me show you around now? I’ll buy you dinner… though it’ll only be at the cafeteria.”

lines.japanese: 「え…えと…」
lines.english: “I… um…”

lines.japanese: 小春の目が、泳いでる。
lines.english: Koharu’s eyes darted helplessly.

lines.japanese:
そして武也の目は…
疑惑の色すら浮かべていない。
lines.english: And Takeya’s eyes… held not even a trace of suspicion.

lines.japanese:
疑っているとかそういうレベルを通り越して、
嘘だってことを確信してる、強い光。
lines.english: They had gone far beyond suspicion. The hard gleam in them said he knew with absolute certainty that I was lying.

lines.japanese:
「行こう。
…武也、そういう訳で、悪いけど」
lines.english:
“Let’s go.
…Sorry, Takeya, but that’s how it is.”

lines.japanese: 「春希…」
lines.english: “Haruki…”

lines.japanese:
けど今は、そんなことに怯む訳にはいかない。
これを事実として、突き進むしかない。
lines.english: But I couldn’t let that stop me. I had to treat the lie as fact and press on.

lines.japanese: 「さ、ほら、行くよ」
lines.english: “Come on. Let’s go.”

lines.japanese: 「先輩…」
lines.english: “But…”

lines.japanese:
「じゃあな武也。
また電話するから」
lines.english: “See you, Takeya. I’ll call you later.”

lines.japanese:
「なぁ春希…
来週のパーティ…ちゃんと来いよ？」
lines.english:
“Haruki…
You’re coming to the party next week. Right?”

lines.japanese:
武也の、なんだか切なそうな声にも、
俺はもう振り返ることができずに、
ただ軽く手を上げて応える。
lines.english: I couldn’t turn around even at the plaintive note in Takeya’s voice. I only raised a hand in reply.

lines.japanese:
そのまま小春の背中を押すようにして、
来た方向と逆に…大学の中へと歩いていく。
lines.english: I ushered Koharu along with a hand at her back and walked the opposite way from where I’d come—back into the university.

lines.japanese:
友達に、背を向けて。
ただひたすら、先の見えない闇の中にまっすぐ。
lines.english: I turned my back on my friend and walked straight into a darkness whose end I couldn’t see.

lines.japanese:
だって…
今ここで、絶対に小春を一人にしちゃいけない。
lines.english: Because… I absolutely could not leave Koharu alone right now.

lines.japanese: ただ、その直感だけは信じられたから。
lines.english: That single instinct, at least, I trusted.

lines.japanese: 「先輩って、時々怖いです…」
lines.english: “You scare me sometimes.”

lines.japanese: 「どこが？」
lines.english: “How?”

lines.japanese:
「いつもは馬鹿がつくくらい正直なのに、
嘘をつくときは容赦ないから」
lines.english:
“You’re normally honest to a fault,
but when you do lie, you’re absolutely ruthless.”

lines.japanese: 「…そうかな」
lines.english: “…You think?”

lines.japanese:
「最初は、ほら…
小木曽先輩のことを一緒に探してた時。
お店の人とか、幹事の人を脅して…」
lines.english: “The first time was when we went looking for Ogiso together. You threatened the people at the restaurant, and the party organizer…”

lines.japanese: 「あったなぁ…そんなこと」
lines.english: “Oh, yeah… That did happen.”

lines.japanese:
俺が小春の、お節介という名の献身を、
初めて自分の身に受けた日のことだ…
lines.english: The day I first became the beneficiary of Koharu’s selfless devotion—otherwise known as meddling…

lines.japanese:
「よくあんな口から出任せが次から次へと出ますね。
…友達相手に。
…全部わたしのせいなのに」
lines.english: “I don’t know how you improvise one outrageous lie after another. To your own friend… all because of me.”

lines.japanese: 「酷いよな、俺…」
lines.english: “I’m awful, aren’t I?”

lines.japanese:
こういう時に、痛感してしまう…
俺は、とんでもない嘘つきなんだって。
lines.english: At times like this, the truth came home to me: I was a consummate liar.

lines.japanese:
大切な人には誠実でいたいとか言いながら、
その大切な人を平気で欺く詐欺師なんだって。
lines.english: I said I wanted to be honest with the people I loved, yet I was a con man who could deceive those very people without a qualm.

lines.japanese:
「ううん、酷いのはわたしです。
…ごめんなさい」
lines.english: “No. I’m the awful one. I’m sorry.”
“…For what?”

lines.japanese: 「ごめんなさぁい…っ」
lines.english: “I’m so sorry…”

lines.japanese: 参ったよなぁ…
lines.english: She really had me at a loss…

lines.japanese: 「待つって約束だったのに…ごめんなさい」
lines.english: “I promised I would wait. I’m sorry.”

lines.japanese: テスト期間中とは言え、夕方とは言え…
lines.english: Granted, it was exam season. Granted, it was evening…

lines.japanese:
「先輩の試験が終わるまで我慢するって…
自分で言ったのに、全然、守れなくなっちゃって」
lines.english: “I said I would hold out until your exams were over. I said it myself, and then I couldn’t keep my word at all.”

lines.japanese: まだ普通に目の前を何人も歩いてるんだけどな。
lines.english: There were still plenty of people walking right past us.

lines.japanese:
「気がついたらあそこにいたんです…
本当に、そんなつもり全然なかったんです」
lines.english: “Before I knew it, I was standing there. I truly never meant to go.”

lines.japanese: 「わかってるって…」
lines.english: “I know.”

lines.japanese:
「ううん、わかってないです先輩。
だって、わたし今、嘘ついてる」
lines.english: “No, you don’t. You don’t understand—I’m lying to you right now.”

lines.japanese: 「小春…」
lines.english: “Koharu…”

lines.japanese:
「あんなところで待ってたら、みんなに見られる。
飯塚先輩にも、水沢先輩にも…
もしかしたら、小木曽先輩にだって」
lines.english: “Waiting somewhere like that, anyone could see me. Takeya could. Io could… even Ogiso might have.”

lines.japanese:
「そのこと、気づいてない訳じゃなかった。
気づいてて、それでも来たんです。
…余計に、タチが悪いんです」
lines.english: “It isn’t as if I didn’t realize that. I knew, and I came anyway. That only makes it worse.”

lines.japanese: 「それは、嘘じゃないって」
lines.english: “That doesn’t make what you said a lie.”

lines.japanese:
「嘘ですよ…
酷い裏切りです。
それも、先輩に対しての」
lines.english: “It does… It was a terrible betrayal. A betrayal of you.”

lines.japanese:
それは嘘じゃなくて…
ただ、判断できなかっただけ。
lines.english: It wasn’t a lie. She simply hadn’t been able to choose.

lines.japanese:
予測できる危険よりも、
ほんの少し、欲望の方が勝ってしまっただけ。
lines.english: Her desire had outweighed the danger she could foresee, if only by a fraction.

lines.japanese: 「な、小春」
lines.english: “Koharu.”

lines.japanese: 「は、はい」
lines.english: “Y-yes?”

lines.japanese:
そんな小春の心の内を、
全部知ってる訳じゃ全然ないんだけど。
lines.english: Not that I came anywhere close to knowing everything in Koharu’s heart.

lines.japanese: 「今から、どこ行こうか？」
lines.english: “Where should we go now?”

lines.japanese: 「先輩…」
lines.english: “Haruki…”

lines.japanese:
「嘘から出た誠で、キャンパス案内してもいいし、
約束通り、学食で晩飯おごってもいい。
…いや、ファミレス程度なら外に出ても構わない」
lines.english: “We can turn our cover story into the truth and tour the campus. I can buy you dinner at the cafeteria like I promised. Or we could even go somewhere off campus, as long as you don’t mind a family restaurant.”

lines.japanese: 「先輩ぃ…っ」
lines.english: “Haruki…!”

lines.japanese:
「だからぁ、泣くなって。
…せめて、二人きり以外の時は」
lines.english: “Come on, don’t cry. At least not while other people are around.”

lines.japanese: 参ったよなぁ…
lines.english: She really had me at a loss…

lines.japanese:
「っ…ぃ、ごめん、なさい。
すいません」
lines.english: “I-I’m sorry. I’m so sorry.”

lines.japanese: テスト期間中とは言え、夕方とは言え…
lines.english: Granted, it was exam season. Granted, it was evening…

lines.japanese: 「ほら、もっとこっち寄っていいから」
lines.english: “Here. You can come closer.”

lines.japanese: まだ普通に目の前を何人も歩いてるんだけどな。
lines.english: There were still plenty of people walking right past us.

lines.japanese:
「は…ぁぃ。
失礼します…っ」
lines.english: “O-okay… if you don’t mind.”

lines.japanese:
そんな衆人環視の中で、
なんで俺、付属の制服姿の女の子の頭を撫でてるんだ…
lines.english: Why was I standing here in full public view, stroking the hair of a girl in a Houjou High uniform?

lines.japanese: 肩まで、抱きながら。
lines.english: With my arm around her shoulders, no less.

lines.japanese: 「…少し落ち着くまで、ここにいるか？」
lines.english: “…Would you rather stay here until you’ve calmed down?”

lines.japanese:
「ぃ、ぃぇ…大丈夫ですから。
これ以上ここにいると、先輩の迷惑になるし」
lines.english: “N-no, I’m all right. If we stay here any longer, I’ll only cause you more trouble.”

lines.japanese:
なんて言いながらも、
肩に乗せた頭をどけるようなことはしないけど…
lines.english: Yet for all she said that, she made no move to lift her head from my shoulder…

lines.japanese:
「じゃ…どこに行く？
どこでも案内するぞ」
lines.english: “Then… where do you want to go? I’ll take you anywhere.”

lines.japanese: 「本当に、どこでもいいんですか？」
lines.english: “Anywhere I want?”

lines.japanese: 「ま、近場なら」
lines.english: “As long as it isn’t too far.”

lines.japanese:
「…近いです。
歩いて行けるはずです」
lines.english: “…It’s close. We should be able to walk.”

lines.japanese:
「そっか…
行き先決まってるんなら、そろそろ行こうか」
lines.english: “I see… If you know where you want to go, we may as well get moving.”

lines.japanese:
「あの…ごめんなさい。
最初に謝っておきます」
lines.english: “Um… I’m sorry. I want to apologize in advance.”

lines.japanese: 「だからもう今までのことは…」
lines.english: “I told you, everything up to now is—”

lines.japanese:
「今までのことじゃなくて…
たった今、先輩を騙したことに」
lines.english: “Not for anything up to now. For the way I just deceived you.”

lines.japanese: 「…遠いの？」
lines.english: “…Is it far after all?”

lines.japanese: 「いえ、そっちじゃなくて…行き先の方」
lines.english: “No, not that. I mean I deceived you about our destination.”

lines.japanese: と、小春は、俺の肩に乗せていた頭をゆっくり持ち上げる。
lines.english: Koharu slowly lifted her head from my shoulder.

lines.japanese:
そして、誰にも話の内容が漏れないよう、
俺の耳に息が届くくらい、口を近づけた…
lines.english: Then she brought her lips so close to my ear that I felt her breath, ensuring no one else could hear.

lines.japanese: 「………先輩の部屋」
lines.english: “………Your room.”

lines.japanese: 「お、思った通り、綺麗に片づいてますね」
lines.english: “I-it’s just as neat as I expected.”

lines.japanese: 「まぁ、最低でも週に二回は掃除してるし」
lines.english: “Well, I clean at least twice a week.”

lines.japanese:
「わ、でも食材は結構入ってる。
一人暮らしの男の人って
ビールばっかりって聞いてたけど」
lines.english: “Oh, you’ve got a lot of groceries too. I’d heard men living alone keep nothing but beer.”

lines.japanese: 「誰に聞いたんだよ…」
lines.english: “Who told you that?”

lines.japanese:
「わ、わ、お風呂場もちゃんと洗ってある。
しかも水洗いじゃなくてちゃんと洗剤使って」
lines.english: “Oh, wow, you actually scrub the bathroom. With cleaner, too, not just a rinse.”

lines.japanese: 「そこは週一回くらいだけど…小春」
lines.english: “I only do that about once a week, but… Koharu.”

lines.japanese:
「わ、わ、わ、結構夜景綺麗。
あ、でもここ寒い…それにエアコンの室外機の音が…」
lines.english: “Wow, the night view’s lovely. Oh, but it’s cold out here… and the air-conditioner unit is loud…”

lines.japanese: 「小春！」
lines.english: “Koharu!”

lines.japanese:
「…落ち着けって。
それに小春の言う通り、寒いから閉めて」
lines.english: “…Calm down. And you’re right, it’s cold, so close the door.”

lines.japanese:
…寒い寒いと言いながら、
額に汗がびっしょり。
lines.english: For all her talk of how cold it was, her forehead was drenched in sweat.

lines.japanese:
「いつまでも立ってないで。
まず座って」
lines.english: “Don’t stand there forever. Sit down.”

lines.japanese:
なんて予想通りにガチガチに緊張してくれるんだ…
そんなことされたら、俺まで緊張してしまう。
lines.english: Of course she’d be wound this tight… Watching her was enough to make me nervous too.

lines.japanese: 「お…お邪魔、します」
lines.english: “Th-thank you for having me.”

lines.japanese:
今ごろになって、普段は絶対忘れない挨拶を
まだしていないことを思い出し、またしても赤面…
lines.english: Only now did she remember the greeting she would ordinarily never forget, and her face turned red all over again.

lines.japanese: 「いや、そこは…」
lines.english: “No, not there…”

lines.japanese: 「え…あ、ああっ！？」
lines.english: “What…? Oh!”

lines.japanese:
…それだけならまだしも、
俺が用意したテーブルの前のクッションにも気づかず、
いきなりベッドに腰掛けてしまうという大チョンボ。
lines.english: As though that weren’t enough, she failed to notice the cushion I’d set before the table and committed the monumental blunder of sitting directly on the bed.
“Nnngh…”

lines.japanese:
耳まで真っ赤にして俯く小春に、
今度はこっちまで恥ずかしくなってしまう。
lines.english: Koharu bowed her head, scarlet to the tips of her ears, and now I was embarrassed as well.

lines.japanese: 「あ、あの、先輩…」
lines.english: “Um, Haruki…”

lines.japanese: 「な、なんだよ」
lines.english: “Wh-what?”

lines.japanese: 「なに、しましょう？」
lines.english: “What shall we do?”

lines.japanese: 「な、なにって…」
lines.english: “What do you mean, what…?”

lines.japanese: これじゃまるで中学生のカップルだ…
lines.english: We were acting like a pair of middle-schoolers dating.

lines.japanese:
初めての時だって、
こんな醜態をさらした記憶はないんだけど。
lines.english: I didn’t remember making this much of a fool of myself even my first time.

lines.japanese: 「先輩の…好きなことで、いいんですけど」
lines.english: “We can do… whatever you like.”

lines.japanese:
って、なんで今を、
『初めての時』と比較するんだよ、俺…
lines.english: Wait—why was I comparing this to my “first time”…?

lines.japanese: あのときと同じことを求めてるのか？　今。
lines.english: Was that what I wanted from her now—the same thing as then?

lines.japanese: ………だとしても。
lines.english: ………Even if it was.

lines.japanese:
「…一緒に飯でも作るか？
まだ食べてないし」
lines.english: “…Want to make dinner together? Neither of us has eaten.”
“What…?”

lines.japanese: だとしても、あのときとは違う。
lines.english: Even if it was, this wasn’t the same as then.

lines.japanese: 俺たちには、まだこの先がある。
lines.english: The two of us still had a future.

lines.japanese:
今日が明日に繋がり、
そして未来へと伸びていく可能性だって…
lines.english: Today might lead into tomorrow, and tomorrow might open into all the days beyond it.

lines.japanese:
「とりあえず、
いつもカレー作れるくらいの材料なら揃ってるから。
小春、包丁使える？」
lines.english:
“For now… I always keep enough ingredients around to make curry.
Can you use a knife, Koharu?”

lines.japanese: 「…駄目です」

「あ、使ったことないか…
結構やってそうなイメージあったんだけど」
lines.english: “You’ve never used one? I’d pictured you doing a fair amount of cooking.”

lines.japanese: 「いえ、普段は使えますが、今日は嫌です」
lines.english: “I can ordinarily use one. I just don’t want to today.”

lines.japanese: 「なんで？」
lines.english: “Why?”

lines.japanese:
「わたしが料理に集中しちゃって、
先輩を見ていられなくなるから」
lines.english: “Because I’d concentrate on the cooking and wouldn’t be able to keep looking at you.”

lines.japanese:
「そんなの嫌です…
だって時間がないのに。
ただでさえ、先輩の貴重な時間削ってるのに」
lines.english: “I don’t want that… We hardly have any time. I’m already taking so much precious study time away from you.”

lines.japanese:
けれど小春は、今日限定の二人きりで過ごせる短い時間に、
無駄な思考を介入させるつもりは一切ないみたいだった。
lines.english:
But with our time alone limited to this one day,
Koharu seemed determined not to let a single stray thought intrude.

lines.japanese:
「…ジャガイモの皮剥きながらだって、
話はできるだろ？」
lines.english: “You can talk while you peel potatoes, can’t you?”

lines.japanese:
「わたし、一つのことにしか集中できないんです。
絶対に思いっきり無言になっちゃいます」
lines.english: “I can only focus on one thing at a time. I’d go completely silent.”

lines.japanese:
それは…思いっきりありそうだ。
このコの場合。
lines.english: That… was all too easy to imagine, with her.

lines.japanese:
「だからわたし…
今日は、先輩に集中してる必要があるんです。
あ、先輩は自由にしていただいても構いません」
lines.english: “So today… I need to focus on you. You’re free to do as you please, of course.”

lines.japanese: 「それって…どうすればいいんだ？」
lines.english: “And what exactly am I supposed to do?”

lines.japanese: 「ええと…試験勉強しててもいいですよ」
lines.english: “Well… you could study for your exams.”

lines.japanese: 「俺が勉強してる間、小春は？」
lines.english: “And while I’m studying, what will you do?”

lines.japanese: 「ずっとその横顔見てます」
lines.english: “I’ll just sit beside you and watch you the whole time.”

lines.japanese:
「あ、思ったよりいいですねそれ。
そしたらわたし、先輩にそれほど迷惑かけなくても…」
lines.english: “Oh, that sounds better than I expected. Then I wouldn’t have to inconvenience you quite so—”

lines.japanese: 「そんなことできるか！」
lines.english: “How could I possibly study with you staring at me?”
“Oh…”

lines.japanese: 何が『先輩の好きなこと』だ…
lines.english: So much for “whatever you like”…

lines.japanese:
さっきから全然、俺のやりたい通りに
やらせてくれないじゃないか。
lines.english: She hadn’t let me do a single thing my way since we got here.

lines.japanese:
やっぱお互い仕切り屋だと、
この辺はどうしてもぶつかり合ってしまうな…
lines.english: This was what happened when two control freaks tried to manage each other.

lines.japanese:
「小春が俺に集中するなら、
俺も小春に集中するしかない。
…でないと気になってしょうがないだろ」
lines.english: “If you’re focusing on me, I have to focus on you. Otherwise I’ll never be able to think about anything else.”

lines.japanese:
「わたしに…集中するんですか？
先輩も？」
lines.english: “You’ll… focus on me? You too?”

lines.japanese: 「小春…」
lines.english: “Koharu…”

lines.japanese: 「んっ…」
lines.english: “Mm…”

lines.japanese:
お互いがお互いを見つめることに集中してしまったら、
二人の距離がなくなってしまうのに、時間はかからない。
lines.english: Once we did nothing but gaze at each other, it didn’t take long for the distance between us to disappear.

lines.japanese: 「ん、んぅ…んぷ…は、あむ…んっ」
lines.english: “Mm… mmm… mph… ah… mm…”

lines.japanese:
小春が目を閉じたのが先か、
俺が唇を触れたのが先か…

lines.japanese: 「心の準備ができてないなら、その…」

こんな時に正論が返ってくるところが、

lines.english: Perhaps her ability to answer with plain good sense at a moment like this was what made her so strong under pressure.

lines.japanese:

lines.japanese: 「だから今は、雪菜のことじゃない」

lines.japanese:

lines.japanese: 「わたし…？」

lines.english: “Whether I should pull you closer and hold you, or stay this far away and keep looking at you.”

それとも、お互いの問題が解決するまで

lines.english: Or whether we should really put a little more distance between us until we’d each resolved our own problems…

lines.japanese: 小春は、話さないから。

自分がどれだけ辛くて、苦しくて、

今日みたいに、

lines.english: Because she only ever revealed any of it through cryptic behavior like today’s.

lines.japanese: 「先輩は…自分がどうしたいってのはないんですか？」

lines.japanese: 「…あるよ」
lines.english: “…I do.”

lines.japanese:

lines.english: “Don’t you want my body? I know my breasts are small… and maybe I wouldn’t be much fun in bed…”

lines.japanese:

lines.english:
“I do…
Your body’s cute, Koharu.

lines.japanese: 「だったら！」
lines.english: “Then!”

lines.english: “But what I want most right now is to do whatever will make you feel safest.”

lines.japanese: 「…やっぱ、優柔不断だって思うか？」
lines.english: “…Do you think that makes me hopelessly indecisive?”

lines.japanese:
「じゃあわたしは…

lines.english: “Then I want to do whatever will make you feel better.”

lines.japanese: 「小春が笑顔を見せてくれれば、俺は元気になれる」
lines.english: “Seeing you smile would make me feel better.”

lines.japanese: 「先輩が元気になれば、わたしは笑顔を見せます」

lines.english: “But I need you to—”

lines.english: “And I need you to—”

lines.japanese: お互い、顔を見合わせてふっと笑い合う。
lines.english: We looked at each other and broke into soft laughter.

lines.japanese:
けれど今度は、

lines.english: This time, though, Koharu didn’t close her eyes, and I made no move to kiss her.

lines.japanese: 「いつまでこんなこと続けるんでしょうね」
lines.english: “How long are we going to keep this up?”

lines.japanese:
「こんなことしてるうちに、
終電の時間になったりしてな」
lines.english: “At this rate, we’ll still be arguing when the last train leaves.”

lines.japanese:
お互い、相手の強情さに呆れつつ、
お互いを思いやる気持ちを知り、
なんとなく板挟みになってるから。
lines.english: We each knew the other was only trying to be considerate, but we were both too stubborn to yield. So we found ourselves at an impasse.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ先輩…平等に行きましょうか？」
lines.english: “Then shall we make it perfectly fair?”

lines.japanese: 「どうやって？」
lines.english: “How?”

lines.japanese: 「いっせ～の、せっ、で」
lines.english: “We’ll say it together on three.”

lines.japanese: 「したいか、したくないか」
lines.english: “Whether we want to do it or not.”

lines.japanese: 「本気か…？」
lines.english: “You’re serious?”

lines.japanese: 「いっせ～の」
lines.english: “Ready…”

lines.japanese:
「って、ちょっと待て！

lines.japanese:
「じゃあ早く決めてください。

lines.english: “Then decide quickly. I already know my answer.”

lines.japanese: 「こ、小春…」
lines.english: “K-Koharu…”

lines.japanese: なんか目が据わってる…

さっきまで、とろんとして滅茶苦茶色っぽかったのに、

lines.japanese:
女って…一瞬でこんなに変わるものなのか。

lines.english: “…Please hurry.”

lines.japanese: 奥が深い…

lines.english: “All right… here we go.”

lines.english: “All right…”

lines.english: The thirty seconds Koharu gave me felt like less than three.

lines.japanese: …まぁ、向こうが時間をサバ読んでた可能性もあるけど。
lines.english: …Though she may have fudged the count.

lines.japanese:
「それじゃ…
いっせ～の…」
lines.english: “All right, then… Ready…”

lines.english: “K-Kitahara… ahh… mmm… haa… haa…”

lines.english: “I’m relaxing in your bath while a man hand-washes all my clothes, right down to my underwear.”

lines.japanese: 「…なんとか明日までには乾かすから」

lines.english: Had I taken responsibility…? And how, exactly?

lines.japanese:
「結局、泊まらざるを得なくなりましたね。

lines.english: “Now I have no choice but to stay over. You were right—calling home beforehand was a good idea.”

lines.japanese: 「はは…」

lines.english:
Once we were done, I hurriedly ran a bath,

lines.english: Once I heard the shower running, I gathered up the clothes I had taken off her, carried them to the washroom, and prepared to hand-wash them in lukewarm water and liquid detergent.

lines.japanese:
…しようとした時に、

lines.english: …That was when I finally realized I was stark naked.

lines.japanese: 「ねぇ、先輩」
lines.english: “Hey.”

lines.english: “Even after you’re married, I imagine you’ll be meticulous about the housework.”

lines.english: “Wh-wh-what are you talking about?!”

lines.english: “Would you be okay with both of you working? Or would you want your wife to stay home?”

lines.english: …For casual conversation, she certainly kept asking difficult questions.

lines.english: “Or my wife could make a fortune while I stay home and run the house.”

lines.english: “I wonder if you could ever give up your career.”

「そんなの働いてみなければわかんないだろ。

lines.english: “How would I know before I’ve even started working? I’m still a student.”

lines.japanese:
「でも、今のバイト先での働きぶりとか見てると、
家でのんびりテレビ見ながら
奥さんの帰りを待ってる先輩って想像できない」
lines.english: “Judging from the way you work now, I can’t picture you lounging in front of the television while you wait for your wife to come home.”

lines.japanese: 「…世の専業主婦を敵に回すなよ予備軍」
lines.english: “Careful, future homemaker. You’re making enemies of every stay-at-home wife in the country.”

lines.japanese: そりゃ、俺だって想像できるわけがないけど。
lines.english: Not that I could picture it either.

lines.japanese:
「先輩って、イメージ的には
『仕事と家庭、どっちを取る？』って聞かれたら、
平気で『どっちも』って答えそう」
lines.english: “You strike me as the sort of person who would be asked, ‘Career or family?’ and answer ‘both’ without hesitation.”

lines.japanese: 反論のしようがない。
lines.english: There was no arguing with that.

lines.japanese:
「ね？　だから早死にしないでね先輩…
わたし、そんなの嫌ですからね？」
lines.english: “So please don’t die young. I couldn’t bear that, all right?”

lines.japanese: なんで小春が嫌がるんだよ…
lines.english: Why would Koharu care…?

lines.japanese:
「その台詞、
そっくりそのまま小春に返してやるから」
lines.english: “I could say exactly the same thing to you.”

lines.japanese: …なんて、言えるわけがない。
lines.english: …As though I could say that.

lines.japanese:
「あは、そうですね…
わたしも気をつけないと」
lines.english: “Ah, I suppose that’s true. I’ll have to be careful too.”

lines.japanese:
だって俺、
小春に早死にされるなんて、絶対嫌だ。
lines.english: Because I absolutely could not bear the thought of Koharu dying young.

lines.japanese:
『もしお母さんが死んだらどうする？』と母親に聞かれ、
どうすることもできずに号泣してしまう幼児のように、
それは理不尽で理屈抜きの感情でしかないけれど…
lines.english: It made no more sense than the terror of a small child who bursts into tears when his mother asks what he’d do if she died…

lines.japanese:
「あ～…いい気持ち。
なんだかこのまま寝ちゃいそう」
lines.english: “Ah… this feels wonderful. I could fall asleep right here.”

lines.japanese:
「別に寝てもいいぞ。
ちゃんとベッドに運んどいてやるから」
lines.english: “Go ahead. I’ll carry you to bed.”

lines.japanese: 「あはは…その時はよろしくお願いしま～す」
lines.english: “Ahaha… I’ll hold you to that.”

lines.japanese:
「お安い御用だ。
何しろ小春、軽いからなぁ」
lines.english: “No trouble at all. You hardly weigh anything.”

lines.japanese: 「先輩はすっごく重かったですよ？」
lines.english: “You were extremely heavy.”

lines.japanese: 「………誠に申し訳ない」
lines.english: “………My profound apologies.”

lines.japanese: 「あはは…あははははっ」
lines.english: “Ahaha… ahahahaha!”

lines.japanese:
でもよかった…
俺の判断は、間違ってなかった。
lines.english: What a relief… I’d made the right choice.

lines.japanese:
だって今、小春が笑ってくれている。
俺の側で、力を抜いて、笑顔を見せてくれている。
lines.english: Koharu was laughing now. Relaxed at my side, she was smiling for me.

lines.japanese:
今の俺にとって、
そのことに勝る安らぎは、この世に存在しない…
lines.english: At that moment, nothing in the world could have brought me greater peace.

lines.japanese: はずだったのに。
lines.english: Or so I thought.

lines.japanese: 「ぅ…ぅぅ…ぅぁぁぁぁ…っ」
lines.english: “Nn… nnngh… aaah…”

lines.japanese: 「小春…おい、小春？」
lines.english: “Koharu? Hey, Koharu?”

lines.japanese:
「ううぅ…うああぁぁぁ…
あ”～っ！　いやああぁぁぁぁぁぁ～っ！」
lines.english: “No… nooo… Aah! No! Nooooo!”

lines.japanese:
「落ち着け！
大丈夫だから、ここは俺の部屋だから！」
lines.english: “Calm down! You’re safe. This is my room!”

lines.japanese:
「せ、先輩…先輩？
い、いぅ…っ、う、う、いぅぃぃい…っ、
いぐっ、う、ぃぅぁぁああああ…っ」
lines.english: “K-Kitahara…? Kitahara? I-I… ngh… aaah…”

lines.japanese:
「わあああああああ～っ！
いあああぁぁっ、うぅぅぃぃ…う～っ！」
lines.english: “Aaaaaah! No… noooo!”

lines.japanese:
どれだけ強く抱きしめても…
何度も『いいこいいこ』をしても…
lines.english: No matter how tightly I held her, no matter how many times I stroked her hair and murmured, “There, there…”

lines.japanese:
「なんで、なんで…
ふえええぇぇぇぇぇ～っ！
いっ、いぅっ…う、う、あ…あぁぁ…っ」
lines.english: “Why? Why…? Nooooo… I… I… aaah…”

lines.japanese:
一度、爆ぜてしまった感情は、
小春を激しく飲み込んでいった。
lines.english: Once the feelings had broken loose, they engulfed Koharu completely.

lines.japanese:
『ここが一番安心できます』って…
俺の胸に顔を埋め、何度も息を吸い込んだ小春。
lines.english: Koharu had buried her face against my chest, breathing me in again and again as she murmured, “This is where I feel safest.”

lines.japanese:
ほどいた髪を梳くように撫でていると、
本当に幸せそうなため息をついた小春。
lines.english: When I combed my fingers through her loosened hair, she’d sighed with such unmistakable happiness.

lines.japanese:
激しく抱いても、覚悟を見せても、
彼女の想いを受け入れても…
lines.english: But no matter how passionately I made love to her, how clearly I showed my commitment, how completely I accepted her feelings…

lines.japanese:
一度できてしまった深い傷が、
そんなに簡単に癒えるわけがなかった…
lines.english: A wound that deep could never have healed so easily.

lines.japanese: 「お邪魔しました」
lines.english: “Thank you for having me.”

lines.japanese: そして、夜が明けて…
lines.english: And then dawn came…

lines.japanese:
そこには、少しだけはれぼったい目をした、
けれど、ほぼ普段通りの小春がいた。
lines.english: Koharu’s eyes were a little swollen, but otherwise she looked almost entirely herself again.

lines.japanese:
なんとか乾いた制服を身にまとい、
鞄を両手で持ち、ぺこりと頭を下げる。
lines.english: Dressed in the uniform we’d managed to dry, she held her bag in both hands and bowed.

lines.japanese:
「昨夜はごめんなさい…
色々と迷惑をかけちゃって」
lines.english: “I’m sorry about last night. I caused you so much trouble.”

lines.japanese: 「そんなことは…」
lines.english: “You didn’t—”

lines.japanese:
「言うの忘れてた…
わたし、暗くして寝るの全然ダメなんです」
lines.english: “I forgot to mention it… I can’t sleep in the dark.”

lines.japanese: 嘘だ。
lines.english: A lie.

lines.japanese:
「子供の頃から暗闇が苦手で、
ふとしたことでスイッチが入ると、
あんなふうになっちゃうんです」
lines.english: “I’ve been frightened of the dark since I was little. Sometimes something sets me off, and I end up like that.”

lines.japanese: 絶対嘘だ。
lines.english: An absolute lie.

lines.japanese: 「…ただ、それだけのことです」
lines.english: “…That’s all it was.”

lines.japanese:
そんなの、あからさまにバレてるのに、
それでも小春は、ただの恐がりで押し通す。
lines.english: The lie was painfully transparent, yet Koharu stuck to the story that she was simply afraid of the dark.

lines.japanese: …昨日の俺みたいに。
lines.english: …Just as I had yesterday.

lines.japanese:
「もう少しゆっくりしてっても…
今日は休みなんだし」
lines.english: “You could stay a little longer. It’s your day off.”

lines.japanese: 「バイト入れてるから」
lines.english: “I have a shift.”

lines.japanese:
「まだ開店まで２時間以上ある。
ここからなら１５分もあれば…」
lines.english: “The restaurant doesn’t open for over two hours. It’s less than fifteen minutes from here.”

lines.japanese:
「一度家に帰って私服に着替えてから行きます。
…洗いたての制服なんかでそのまま行っちゃったら、
中川さんになんて勘繰られるか」
lines.english: “I’m going home to change first. Imagine what Nakagawa would suspect if I arrived in a freshly washed uniform.”

lines.japanese: 「なら、家まで送…」
lines.english: “Then I’ll walk you—”

lines.japanese:
「ダメですよ。
試験中じゃないですか」
lines.english: “No. You have exams.”

lines.japanese: 「小春…」
lines.english: “Koharu…”

lines.japanese:
「もう、先輩甘いなぁ…
やめてくださいそういうの。
わたし、どんどん弱くなっちゃいそう」
lines.english: “You’re too soft on me… Please don’t be. I’m afraid I’ll just get weaker and weaker.”

lines.japanese:
弱くなったのか、
もともと強くなんかなかったのか…
lines.english: Had she grown weaker? Or had she never been strong to begin with…?

lines.japanese:
俺と知り合った頃は、強いコにしか見えなかった。
俺に介入しだした頃は、優しいコにも見えてきた。
lines.english: When we met, she had seemed nothing but strong. When she began meddling in my life, I started to see her kindness too.

lines.japanese:
そして、俺の側にいるようになってからは、
泣いてばかりだ。
lines.english: And ever since she began staying by my side, all she did was cry.

lines.japanese: 「試験頑張ってくださいね、先輩」
lines.english: “Good luck with your exams.”

lines.japanese: 「うん…」
lines.english: “Mm…”

lines.japanese:
「わたし、次に先輩に会える日だけを指折り数えて、
明日からまた頑張っていきます」
lines.english: “I’ll count down the days until I can see you again. Starting tomorrow, that’s what will keep me going.”

lines.japanese: 「それじゃ…」
lines.english: “Well, then…”

lines.japanese:
小春の、ソックスに包まれた足が、
小さな革靴に包まれる。
lines.english: Koharu slipped her socked feet into her little leather shoes.

lines.japanese:
つま先を軽くトントンと床で叩き、かかとまで覆うと、
ゆっくりと背を向けて、ドアノブに手をかける。
lines.english: She tapped each toe lightly against the floor, settled her heels, then slowly turned away and put her hand on the doorknob.

lines.japanese: 「小春…っ」
lines.english: “Koharu…”

lines.japanese: 「…はい」
lines.english: “…Yes?”

lines.japanese:
俺の呼びかけにも、
小春はノブを握り、後ろを向いたままで応えた。
lines.english: She answered without looking back, her hand still gripping the knob.

lines.japanese: 「こうなったこと…後悔してないか？」
lines.english: “Do you regret what happened between us?”

lines.japanese: 「してません」
lines.english: “No.”

lines.japanese:
「俺と知り合わなければよかったって、
思ったことないか？」
lines.english: “Have you ever wished you’d never met me?”

lines.japanese: 「ありません」
lines.english: “Never.”

lines.japanese:
「冬が来る前の、
矢田さんと仲の良かったあの日に帰りたいって…」
lines.english: “Have you ever wanted to go back to before winter, when you and Yada were still close—”

lines.japanese: 「思いません」
lines.english: “I don’t.”

lines.japanese: 全部、即答だった。
lines.english: Every answer had come without hesitation.

lines.japanese:
最後なんか、質問が終わるよりも前に
自分の気持ちをまっすぐぶつけてきた。
lines.english: The last one had flown straight at me before I even finished the question.

lines.japanese:
…後ろを向いていたから、
ドアにぶつかって、反射してから届いたけれど。
lines.english: …Though since she had her back to me, it struck the door and reached me on the rebound.

lines.japanese: 「先輩は悲観的すぎます」
lines.english: “You’re much too pessimistic.”

lines.japanese:
そんなことを…
昨夜、一時間以上も泣きやめなかった少女が言い放つ。
lines.english: So declared the girl who had cried for over an hour the night before.

lines.japanese:
「こんな、胸が潰れるくらい嬉しい痛みを
知ってしまったら、もう元のわたしには戻れません。
…戻りたいとも思いません」
lines.english:
“Now that I know a joyful ache
powerful enough to crush my heart,
I can never go back to who I was.
…Nor do I want to.”

lines.japanese: 「小春…」
lines.english: “Koharu…”

lines.japanese:
「世の中が何もかも、
このくらい思い通りに行けばいいのにってくらい、
今、素敵な恋をしてるんですよ？　わたし」
lines.english: “I’m in love right now—and it’s so wonderful that I wish everything else in the world could go just as perfectly.”

lines.japanese: 『なんて恥ずかしいこと言うんだ…小春らしくもない』
lines.english: “How can you say something that embarrassing? It isn’t like you at all.”

lines.japanese:
…言えるわけ、ない。
絶対に、言いたくない。
lines.english: …I couldn’t say it. I didn’t want to. Not ever.

lines.japanese:
「わたしの望みが叶ったから、
先輩の望みは遠ざかっちゃったかもしれないですけどね」
lines.english: “I got what I wanted, though. Maybe that’s put what you want even farther out of reach.”

lines.japanese: 「俺の望みは…昨夜叶ったよ」
lines.english: “My wish… came true last night.”

lines.japanese: 「ありがとう、ございます…っ」
lines.english: “Thank you…”

lines.japanese:
そこまで強く思い込んでしまったからこそ、
小春は俺に、何も話してくれないんだろうか。
lines.english: Was it because she believed this so fiercely that Koharu wouldn’t tell me anything?

lines.japanese:
好きだからこそ背負いたいのに、
好きだからこそ背負わせたくないんだろうか。
lines.english: Did I want to shoulder her burdens because I loved her, while she refused to let me shoulder them for precisely the same reason?

lines.japanese:
だとしたらそれは、
相手のためって言う、お互いのエゴのぶつかり合い。
lines.english: If so, this was just two selfish impulses colliding, each in the name of the other.

lines.japanese:
俺たちは、揃いも揃ってわがままで、強情で、
そして、相手のことを誰よりも想ってるって…
lines.english: We were both selfish and stubborn to a fault, and each of us cared about the other more than anyone—

lines.japanese: 誰、よりも…？
lines.english: More than… anyone?

lines.japanese: 「さよなら…」
lines.english: “Goodbye…”
“………Koharu!”

lines.japanese:
「あ…っ、
ん…んぅ…」
lines.english: “Ah… mm…”

lines.japanese:
ドアを開けたら、小春はすぐそこにいた。
…そんなのは、当たり前なんだけど。
lines.english: When I opened the door, Koharu was still right there. Of course she was.

lines.japanese: 「ん…んむ…」
lines.english: “Mmm…”

lines.japanese: 「ん、ん…ちゅ…ぷぁ…は、あ…」
lines.english: “Mm… mmm… ah…”

lines.japanese:
でも、捕まえられたのが嬉しくて、
その小さな身体を抱きしめ、強引に唇を奪った。
lines.english: But I was so glad I’d caught her that I wrapped my arms around her small body and kissed her hard.

lines.japanese:
「先輩…
ここ、外…」
lines.english: “We’re outside…”

lines.japanese:
「行ってこい。
…気をつけてな」
lines.english: “Off you go. Be careful.”
“Oh…”

lines.japanese: 小春の挨拶が気に入らなかったから。
lines.english: I hadn’t liked the way she said goodbye.

lines.japanese:
たとえどんな意味だろうと、
『さよなら』を言って欲しくなかったから。
lines.english: Whatever she might have meant by it, I didn’t want to hear that word from her.

lines.japanese: 「行って、きます？」
lines.english: “I’ll… be back, then?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ」
lines.english: “Yeah.”

lines.japanese: 「行ってきます…」
lines.english: “I’ll be back…”

lines.japanese: 「行ってらっしゃい」
lines.english: “I’ll be here.”

lines.japanese: 「行ってきます！」
lines.english: “I’ll be back!”

lines.japanese: 「またな、小春」
lines.english: “See you soon, Koharu.”

lines.japanese: 「はいっ！」
lines.english: “Yes!”

lines.japanese:
抱きしめたとき、
制服は少しだけ湿っていたけれど…
lines.english: When I held her, her uniform was still a little damp.

lines.japanese:
それでも最後に見せてくれた小春の笑顔は、
冬の朝の突き刺すような寒さにも負けずに、
はっきりと輝いてくれた。
lines.english: But the smile Koharu gave me at the end shone clear and bright, undimmed by the piercing cold of that winter morning.
